parsed.explanation: No visitor-facing restriction is documented: no LGBT border screening, no trans-specific criminal offence, no birth-sex facility or custody rule, no document-mismatch friction, and no organised targeting or trans-specific violence record. Incitement to violence against LGBT people is criminalised, same-sex conduct is legal, and courts actively strike down anti-LGBT restrictions (Dec 2024 speech ruling, 2025 partnership ruling, 2019 residence ruling) — rule of law partly works for LGBT people. Against this: documented police failure to protect an assembly, a systemic hate-crime victim-support gap, a hostile political climate (large anti-partnership protests, head-of-state statements), and recurring hostile bills. Most negatives are resident-facing (no LGR, workplace discrimination). Custody and visitor-service treatment are open questions, not exposures. Net: reduced risk with real friction and thin recourse, not a universal or state-imposed exposure.
